problem_framing.rationale: Frames the decision as 'whether and how', uses the 15% ARR target, NRR above 100% and renewal and cap constraints as explicit tests (slide 3). It tests the CFO hypothesis against what would have to be true. It identifies early that the answer turns on segment, cohort and the real size of the uplift. It lacks an explicit criteria scorecard for the alternatives.

storyline_coherence.rationale: The governing thought, the five summary points and the slide titles line up. The titles are claims and the argument reads from titles alone. Minor flaws: the summary line 'not because customers are reacting to price' sits uneasily with the finding that the promo cohort did react to price. Slide 6's title says core SMB customers are 'no more price-sensitive at renewal than before', but the body says their sensitivity is unknown. 'No SMB exposure' also sits beside a live SMB test.

evidence_and_reasoning.rationale: Numbers check out. Blended churn 1.7→2.6% and ARR-weighted 0.8→1.2%. Promo cohort 4.9% with a ≈1.0pp mix effect. Repriceable $7.57M, with the correct treatment of the 15%, 60% and 7% cap. Net NRR 109.3% and the ARR bridge are correct. The exit-survey cross-check (47% vs 56%) is a thoughtful touch. The dashboard metric is shown not to reconcile. Weaknesses: the 12% break-even (~10.7%) and the 2023 net (~4.1%) are never stated directly (only the 7.4% break-even for +8%). The churn-reaction model is linear with a judgemental 2× promo factor. The slide 6 title overclaims. The $0.9M new-customer need rests on an assumed repeat of trailing NRR, which the document flags.

strategic_judgment.rationale: Differentiated recommendation: mid-market +12% with a fall-back to +10%, enterprise within caps, SMB held and tested, promo cohort exempt. It compares no increase, uniform 12% and targeted on base and downside cases. It has explicit gates (1.0% mid-market churn trigger, SMB test decision thresholds), a timeline and decisions. It corrects the budget line. It rejects the 'halve churn' claim with arithmetic. It avoids all five traps and caveats the new-signup test. Gaps: no lower-priced SMB tier or restructuring option, and only light treatment of renewal trust and brand effects.

clarity_and_concision.rationale: The answer is on slide 2 and the writing is plain. At 18 slides and about 4,600 words, it is long for the decision. The detail on SMB test power and thresholds, the risk table and two appendices could be trimmed. A few slides are dense.

unsupported_claims.quote: Core SMB customers are no more price-sensitive at renewal than before
unsupported_claims.why: Core SMB churn and price-citing shares are flat, but core customers have not faced a price increase since Inkwell launched. The document itself says their sensitivity is unknown.

unsupported_claims.quote: Churn is rising because of one cohort, not because customers are reacting to price.
unsupported_claims.why: Overstated headline. The same deck shows the cohort left over price when the discount ended (52% cite price), and Inkwell is pressuring SMB acquisition.

unsupported_claims.quote: The rise is a one-off effect from one cohort. As the cohort shrinks, blended SMB churn should drift back towards ≈2.1%.
unsupported_claims.why: Assumes the cohort churns out and that core churn stays flat. Inkwell's effect on core churn is not yet observed.

unsupported_claims.quote: SMB NRR stays below 100% (94%) under every option. That is a cohort problem, and price won't fix it.
unsupported_claims.why: Cohort attribution of the NRR shortfall is not derived from the pack, which gives no cohort-level NRR.

logical_contradictions.quote_a: Churn is rising because of one cohort, not because customers are reacting to price.
logical_contradictions.quote_b: This cohort has just shown it is very sensitive to price.
logical_contradictions.why: The summary denies a price reaction, but the body says the cohort that drives the rise left over price. The point is partly reconciled on slide 5 and the slide 3 caveat.

recommendation.summary: Raise prices in 2027 selectively. Mid-market +12% at renewal, falling back to +10% if Q1 churn exceeds 1.0% a month. Enterprise up to contract terms. Hold SMB list prices and exempt the promo cohort. Run a randomised +8% test on core SMB in Q1. Fund onboarding. Reset the budget to $4.1M and define the board churn metric.
recommendation.rationale: It differentiates by segment, separates the cohort mix effect from a rate effect, corrects the $10.3M to about $7.6M repriceable and about $5.0M net, and reconciles the CFO and CEO views. It has gates, a staged test and next steps.

hypothesis_handling.rationale: It tests the CFO hypothesis as a set of conditions. It keeps the part about churn not being a general price reaction and revises the 'every plan at 12%' and '$10.3M' parts. It notes the cohort is price-sensitive, which supports the CEO's worry, and that the CFO is wrong that churn is only onboarding. The result is a segment-differentiated revision. A couple of headline phrasings overstate the 'not price' reading.

output.overall_comment: This is a strong, well-calibrated deck. The mix decomposition, the corrected uplift, the segment split and the alternatives are all handled right. It has clear gates and a staged test. The remaining flaws are small: a few overstated titles, a model of churn reaction built on linear scaling and a judgemental 2× factor, and no explicit 12% break-even or 2023 net-effect figure. It is also longer than the decision strictly needs.
